Fleets & business · 6 minute read

Keeping fleet graphics consistent.

How to keep fleet livery consistent across different makes and models, colour batches, replacements and new vehicles.

Get a free quote Try the Van Designer

At a glance

1master spec covering the whole fleet
3things to agree up front
0mismatched vans on the road

In this guide

  1. Why consistency matters
  2. Create a fleet livery spec
  3. Adapting to different models
  4. Replacements and repairs
Get a free quote

Quick answer

Agree a master set of colours, logo sizes and positions, then adapt it to each model using templates so every vehicle looks like the same company.

01

Why consistency matters

A consistent fleet looks established and is easier to recognise on the road. Vans with different logos, colours or phone numbers look like different businesses and are harder to remember.

02

Create a fleet livery spec

1

Colours

Exact vinyl or print references for every brand colour.

2

Logo rules

Sizes and positions for sides, rear and bonnet.

3

Contact details

One phone number and website used everywhere.

Tip

Keep the spec in one place and share it with anyone who orders vehicles or graphics.

03

Adapting to different models

Panel shapes differ between makes, so the layout is adapted to each model while keeping the same proportions and positions. A Transit Custom and a Vivaro can carry the same livery, adjusted for their doors, handles and glazing.

Keep the same

  • Logo and colours
  • Contact details
  • Order of information
  • Fleet number style

Adjust per model

  • Exact sizes and positions
  • Line breaks in longer text
  • Rear door layout
  • Placement around handles
04

Replacements and repairs

Mixing films

Different films fade at different rates.

Fix: Use the same film for replacements.

Lost artwork

Re-creating files leads to differences.

Fix: Keep master files on record with us.

Ad hoc changes

One-off tweaks spread across the fleet.

Fix: Update the spec, then the vehicles.

What to have ready for your quote

  • Master logo files
  • Colour references
  • List of makes and models
  • Approved contact details
  • Fleet numbering rules
  • Who approves changes
  • Replacement process
  • New vehicles planned

Before you book

Fleet graphics consistency: your questions.

What if we change van models?

The master design is reworked for the new model’s panels, so it sits alongside your other vans.

Can you match graphics another company fitted?

Often, yes. Send photos and any files you have, and we will match the layout and colours as closely as possible.

How do you keep colours the same over time?

We record the exact films and print settings used, so replacements and new vehicles match.
